tagline: Up the shore on Ocean Boulevard, then out to an island.
intro: NH 1A comes up out of Seabrook and over the Hampton Bridge onto Hampton Beach, where Ocean Boulevard runs right beside the sand. North of the boardwalk the building thins out to salt marsh and bungalows, and the road keeps to the shore through North Hampton and Rye, past Rye Harbor, until Odiorne Point. There it turns inland.

At Portsmouth, Route 1B takes the causeway out to New Castle, the only town in New Hampshire set entirely on islands. In 1682 a tavern there was showered all summer with stones thrown, a London pamphlet reported, by an invisible hand.

moments.title: Hampton Beach
moments.text: On a barrier spit across the harbor inlet, 1A splits into one-way streets crossed by streets lettered A to M, and the Casino Ballroom books national acts for the summer.

moments.title: Odiorne Point State Park
moments.text: Where 1A leaves the ocean, the concrete gun platforms of wartime Fort Dearborn remain, and the Seacoast Science Center keeps touch tanks and whale skeletons.

moments.title: Fort Constitution
moments.text: In December 1774 Portsmouth Patriots overpowered the six-man caretaker garrison of this harbor fort and carried off its gunpowder.
